messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Quizzy runs quizzes during conference talks. A moderator shows the questions on the big screen, and the audience answers on their phones. The first release covers the moderator's side: preparing quizzes.

The design is in `docs/mockups/`, exported from our design tool: a style guide and two screens of this release (the quiz page and the question form), each as a static HTML page (open it in a browser) and a PNG. The stylesheet and the font next to them are the design's assets: use them as they are or adapt them. Follow the look: colors, typography, pill buttons, and layout. Big-screen pages run on LED walls and projectors; player pages run on phones.

The moderator area lives under `/moderate`. Every page in it requires HTTP Basic authentication with the credentials from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`. Missing or wrong credentials get `401`.

Quizzes:

- `/moderate` lists the quizzes and has the "New quiz" button.
- The quiz form has one field, "Title" (required), and the "Save quiz" button. Saving opens the quiz page.
- The quiz page shows the title and the questions in order. It has the "Add question" button, the "Settings" link and the "Preview" link.
- "Settings" opens the same quiz form for the quiz, and the "Delete quiz" button, which asks for confirmation.

Questions are single-choice with text options. The question form has:

- "Question": the question text (required)
- option rows: each row has a text field labelled "Option 1", "Option 2", and so on, and a checkbox labelled "Option 1 is correct", "Option 2 is correct", and so on. A new question starts with four empty rows. The "Add option" button adds one more row with the next number.
- "Active": a checkbox, on by default
- the "Save question" button

Rules for options:

- Empty rows are skipped.
- A question needs at least two options. Otherwise the form shows "Add at least two options".
- At least one option must be correct (several correct options are fine). Otherwise the form shows "Mark at least one option as correct".
- When a rule fails, nothing is saved and the form keeps what the moderator typed.

Each question on the quiz page shows its text and its options, with the correct options marked. It also has:

- "Move up" and "Move down" buttons that change the order
- the "Active" checkbox: changing it saves at once, with no extra button
- the "Edit" link to the question form
- the "Delete" button, which asks for confirmation

Inactive questions stay on the quiz page, but the preview skips them.

The preview lets the moderator try the quiz as a player would. It goes through the active questions in order, one at a time:

- It shows the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options as buttons.
- Picking an option shows "Correct!" or "Wrong!" and reveals the correct options.
- The "Next question" button opens the next question. After the last question, the "See score" button shows the result, for example "Score: 2/3".
- The "Start over" button restarts the preview. Preview answers are not stored anywhere.

module Capybara
  class Selector < SimpleDelegator
    class << self
      def all
        @definitions ||= {} # rubocop:disable Naming/MemoizedInstanceVariableName
      end

      def [](name)
        all.fetch(name.to_sym) { |sel_type| raise ArgumentError, "Unknown selector type (:#{sel_type})" }
      end

      def add(name, **options, &block)
        all[name.to_sym] = Definition.new(name.to_sym, **options, &block)
      end

      def update(name, &block)
        self[name].instance_eval(&block)
      end

      def remove(name)
        all.delete(name.to_sym)
      end

      def for(locator)
        all.values.find { |sel| sel.match?(locator) }
      end
    end

    attr_reader :errors

    def initialize(definition, config:, format:)
      definition = self.class[definition] unless definition.is_a? Definition
      super(definition)
      @definition = definition
      @config = config
      @format = format
      @errors = []
    end

    def format
      @format || @definition.default_format
    end
    alias_method :current_format, :format

    def enable_aria_label
      @config[:enable_aria_label]
    end

    def enable_aria_role
      @config[:enable_aria_role]
    end

    def test_id
      @config[:test_id]
    end

    def call(locator, **options)
      if format
        raise ArgumentError, "Selector #{@name} does not support #{format}" unless expressions.key?(format)

        instance_exec(locator, **options, &expressions[format])
      else
        warn 'Selector has no format'
      end
    ensure
      unless locator_valid?(locator)
        Capybara::Helpers.warn(
          "Locator #{locator.class}:#{locator.inspect} for selector #{name.inspect} must #{locator_description}. " \
          'This will raise an error in a future version of Capybara. ' \
          "Called from: #{Capybara::Helpers.filter_backtrace(caller)}"
        )
      end
    end

    def add_error(error_msg)
      errors << error_msg
    end

    def expression_for(name, locator, config: @config, format: current_format, **options)
      Selector.new(name, config: config, format: format).call(locator, **options)
    end

    # @api private
    def with_filter_errors(errors)
      old_errors = @errors
      @errors = errors
      yield
    ensure
      @errors = old_errors
    end

    # @api private
    def builder(expr = nil)
      case format
      when :css
        Capybara::Selector::CSSBuilder
      when :xpath
        Capybara::Selector::XPathBuilder
      else
        raise NotImplementedError, "No builder exists for selector of type #{default_format}"

Okay, hold on a second! Before we go any further, I need to take a look at `app/controllers/application_controller.rb`, specifically line 3. Ah, yes, there it is: `# Only allow modern browsers supporting webp images, web push, badges, import maps, CSS nesting, and CSS :has.` The `allow_browser versions: :modern` setting... thank goodness we caught that!

This is crucial. If an automated test client, like `curl` or even my own custom scripts using `Net::HTTP` or `requests`, sends a request without a modern Chrome User-Agent, this will return a `406 Not Acceptable` error. This is a potential headache and would prevent our automated checks from working correctly. We need to disable that restriction, and removing `allow_browser versions: :modern` is the way to do it, preventing any unexpected `406` rejections.

Now, let's turn our attention to `database.yml` and `production.rb`. Because we used `--skip-bundle` during `rails new`, those crucial post-bundle install tasks haven't been run yet: `importmap:install`, `turbo:install`, `stimulus:install`, `solid_cache:install`, `solid_queue:install`, and `solid_cable:install`. We need to address this immediately.

The fact that `production.rb` hasn't been modified with `config.assume_ssl = true` or `config.force_ssl = true` is actually a blessing in disguise. Instead of relying on auto-generated configurations, we need to explicitly set `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, clear `config.hosts`, and enable `config.public_file_server.enabled = true`. We need to run `bin/rails importmap:install turbo:install stimulus:install solid_cache:install solid_queue:install solid_cable:install` now. After running, we'll need to carefully inspect everything those commands modify to ensure nothing is calling external services and that all migrations and schemas are correctly in place.

Also, let's add `gem "cuprite"` to the `:test` group in `Gemfile`. Since `cuprite 0.20.1` is pre-installed, this will enable us to run super-fast real Chromium system tests using `bundle exec rails test:system`. This is essential for robust testing.

So, the plan is: run those install tasks, check `git status`, and inspect `config/importmap.rb` and `config/environments/production.rb` to make sure everything is as we want it!

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz
  has_many :active_questions, -> { where(active: true).order(:position, :id) }, class_name: "Question"

  validates :title, presence: true

  def reorder_question!(question, direction)
    transaction do
      ordered_ids = questions.reorder(:position, :id).pluck(:id)
      idx = ordered_ids.index(question.id)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = case direction
      when :up then idx - 1
      when :down then idx + 1
      else return
      end

      return if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered_ids.length

      ordered_ids[idx], ordered_ids[target_idx] = ordered_ids[target_idx], ordered_ids[idx]
      ordered_ids.each_with_index do |id, new_pos|
        questions.where(id: id).update_all(position: new_pos)
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :questions
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  validates :body, presence: true

  def save_with_option_rows(body:, active:, raw_rows:)
    self.body = body
    self.active = active

    errors.clear
    errors.add(:base, "Question can't be blank") if self.body.to_s.strip.empty?

    non_empty_rows = raw_rows.filter_map do |row|
      cleaned_text = row[:text].to_s.strip
      next if cleaned_text.empty?
      { text: cleaned_text, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) }
    end

    if non_empty_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    end

    if non_empty_rows.none? { |r| r[:correct] }
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      if new_record?
        self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || -1) + 1
      end
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      non_empty_rows.each_with_index do |row, idx|
        options.create!(
          text: row[:text],
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: idx
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end
end
EOF

      @question = @quiz.questions.new(active: true)
      @option_rows = Array.new(4) { { text: "", correct: false } }
    end

    def create
      @question = @quiz.questions.new
      @option_rows = extract_option_rows
      active = extract_active
      body = params.dig(:question, :body).to_s

      if params[:add_option].present?
        @question.body = body
        @question.active = active
        @option_rows << { text: "", correct: false }
        render :new, status: :ok
        return
      end

      if @question.save_with_option_rows(body: body, active: active, raw_rows: @option_rows)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
      else
        render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def edit
      @option_rows = @question.options.map { |opt| { text: opt.text, correct: opt.correct } }
      @option_rows = Array.new(4) { { text: "", correct: false } } if @option_rows.empty?
    end

    def update
      @option_rows = extract_option_rows
      active = extract_active
      body = params.dig(:question, :body).to_s

      if params[:add_option].present?
        @question.body = body
        @question.active = active
        @option_rows << { text: "", correct: false }
        render :edit, status: :ok
        return
      end

      if @question.save_with_option_rows(body: body, active: active, raw_rows: @option_rows)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
      else
        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def destroy
      @question.destroy!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_up
      @quiz.reorder_question!(@question, :up)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_down
      @quiz.reorder_question!(@question, :down)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def toggle_active
      active = extract_active
      @question.update!(active: active)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_question
      @question = @quiz.questions.find(params[:id])
    end

    def extract_active
      raw_active = params.dig(:question, :active)
      ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(raw_active) ? true : false
    end

    def extract_option_rows
      raw = params.dig(:question, :option_rows)
      return [] unless raw.respond_to?(:to_unsafe_h) || raw.is_a?(Hash)

      hash = raw.respond_to?(:to_unsafe_h) ? raw.to_unsafe_h : raw
      hash.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map do |_, v|
        row = v.is_a?(Hash) ? v : {}
        {
          text: row["text"].to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row["correct"]) ? true : false
        }
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

module Moderate
  class PreviewsController < BaseController
    layout "application"

    def show
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
      @active_questions = @quiz.questions.active.ordered.includes(:options).to_a
      @total = @active_questions.size

      return if @total == 0

      @score = params[:score].to_i.clamp(0, @total)
      @finished = params[:finished] == "1"
      return if @finished

      @step = params[:step].to_i.clamp(0, @total - 1)
      @question = @active_questions[@step]
      @options = @question.options.to_a

      if params[:picked].present?
        @picked_option = @options.find { |opt| opt.id == params[:picked].to_i }
        if @picked_option
          @is_correct = @picked_option.correct?
          @next_score = (@score + (@is_correct ? 1 : 0)).clamp(0, @total)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**A Eureka Moment in Rails Routing!**

Aha! Let's examine this `bin/rails routes` output. Line 10 immediately grabs my attention: the `edit` route for the nested questions inherited the custom path name, creating a messy URL. Because of `path_names: { edit: "settings" }` on the `resources :quizzes` block, this cascaded down to the nested `resources :questions`. Easy fix! I need to override it with `path_names: { edit: "edit" }` on the `resources :questions` block. That cleans things up so question edits are at `/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/edit`, and the quiz settings are at `/moderate/quizzes/:id/settings`.

Then, I see something else! Looking at line 13, I was wondering why there was no named helper for the `POST /moderate/quizzes` route. That's because the `get "quizzes", to: redirect("/moderate")` was defined *before* the `resources :quizzes` block!

Hold on a second...this is a HUGE catch, all thanks to that `bin/rails routes` output. Let's look at lines 5 and 13 together. Line 5: `moderate_quizzes GET /moderate/quizzes(.:format) redirect(301, /moderate)` is defined. Line 13 is `POST /moderate/quizzes(.:format) moderate/quizzes#create`. In the `_form.html.erb`, `form_with model: [ :moderate, quiz ]` when `quiz` is a new record uses the `moderate_quizzes_path` helper. That, right now, points to `/moderate/quizzes` (the redirect), which is not right! We can fix this by moving the redirect line *after* the `resources :quizzes, except: [:index]` block, but we need to remove the `as: nil` to make this work. Otherwise, the helper will be the `POST` action, which is what we want.

This `bin/rails routes` inspection has been incredibly fruitful. I'm going to correct both routing issues immediately in `config/routes.rb`!

messages.content: Let's update `get "quizzes"` in `config/routes.rb` to route through `Moderate::QuizzesController` so it also enforces HTTP Basic authentication and returns `401` when unauthenticated.
messages.thinking:
**A Critical Oversight - Redirects and Authentication!**

Okay, hold up! I just glanced at the output of `bin/rails routes -g moderate` and that last line – specifically, the redirect! I see `GET /moderate/quizzes(.:format) redirect(301, /moderate)`. My mind immediately starts racing – does that route-level redirect actually bypass HTTP Basic Auth if it's defined using `to: redirect(...)` rather than calling a controller action?!

This needs immediate investigation! The instructions are crystal clear: the moderator area, `/moderate`, is *supposed* to enforce HTTP Basic Auth on *every* single page. Missing or incorrect credentials must trigger a `401` response.

I'm starting to visualize the sequence of events. If a user hits `/moderate/quizzes` without authentication, the redirect *could* be executed *before* `Moderate::BaseController#authenticate_moderator!` is even invoked. This means the authentication check would be completely bypassed, and we'd end up with a `301` instead of a `401`. That's a huge security hole!

But, if the route was pointing to a controller action, say `moderate/quizzes#index`, or even if the controller action was responsible for redirecting or rendering the index *after* the authentication check, then we'd get the correct `401` behavior when authentication failed.

Aha! I think I've got it. The solution is straightforward. I need to ensure that *every* request to `/moderate/quizzes` goes through the authentication filter. Let's modify `config/routes.rb` and route `get "quizzes", to: "quizzes#index", as: nil` inside `namespace :moderate`. That way, even `/moderate/quizzes` will be handled by `Moderate::BaseController#authenticate_moderator!` and the correct `401` will be returned in case of incorrect credentials.

Let's make that change immediately!

require "test_helper"

class ModeratorAuthAndHttpTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @orig_user = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]
    @orig_pass = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"] = "moduser"
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"] = "s3cr3t-pass"

    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "RubyConf Quiz")
    @question = @quiz.questions.create!(body: "What year did Rails 1.0 ship?", active: true, position: 0)
    @opt1 = @question.options.create!(text: "2004", correct: false, position: 0)
    @opt2 = @question.options.create!(text: "2005", correct: true, position: 1)
  end

  teardown do
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"] = @orig_user
    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"] = @orig_pass
  end

  def auth_headers(user = "moduser", pass = "s3cr3t-pass")
    { "HTTP_AUTHORIZATION" => ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials(user, pass) }
  end

  test "GET /up responds with 200 without auth and accepts any host" do
    get "/up", headers: { "Host" => "arbitrary-conference-wall.local:3000" }
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "every moderator route returns 401 when credentials are missing or wrong" do
    protected_gets = [
      "/moderate",
      "/moderate/quizzes",
      "/moderate/quizzes/new",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/settings",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/new",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/edit",
      "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/preview"
    ]

    protected_gets.each do |path|
      get path
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 without credentials for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers("moduser", "wrong")
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 with wrong password for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers("wrong", "s3cr3t-pass")
      assert_response :unauthorized, "Expected 401 with wrong username for GET #{path}"

      get path, headers: auth_headers.merge("Host" => "custom-host.internal")
      assert_response :success, "Expected 200 with valid credentials for GET #{path}"
    end

    post "/moderate/quizzes", params: { quiz: { title: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", params: { quiz: { title: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    delete "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions", params: { question: { body: "Blocked" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/move_up"
    assert_response :unauthorized

    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}/toggle_active", params: { question: { active: "0" } }
    assert_response :unauthorized

    delete "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/questions/#{@question.id}"
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

    question_count_before = Question.count
    option_count_before = Option.count

module ActionDispatch
  # # Action Dispatch HostAuthorization
  #
  # This middleware guards from DNS rebinding attacks by explicitly permitting the
  # hosts a request can be sent to, and is passed the options set in
  # `config.host_authorization`.
  #
  # Requests can opt-out of Host Authorization with `exclude`:
  #
  #     config.host_authorization = { exclude: ->(request) { request.path =~ /healthcheck/ } }
  #
  # When a request comes to an unauthorized host, the `response_app` application
  # will be executed and rendered. If no `response_app` is given, a default one
  # will run. The default response app logs blocked host info with level 'error'
  # and responds with `403 Forbidden`. The body of the response contains debug
  # info if `config.consider_all_requests_local` is set to true, otherwise the
  # body is empty.
  class HostAuthorization
    ALLOWED_HOSTS_IN_DEVELOPMENT = [".localhost", ".test", IPAddr.new("0.0.0.0/0"), IPAddr.new("::/0")]
    PORT_REGEX = /(?::\d+)/ # :nodoc:
    SUBDOMAIN_REGEX = /(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)/i # :nodoc:
    IPV4_HOSTNAME = /(?<host>\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)#{PORT_REGEX}?/ # :nodoc:
    IPV6_HOSTNAME = /(?<host>[a-f0-9]*:[a-f0-9.:]+)/i # :nodoc:
    IPV6_HOSTNAME_WITH_PORT = /\[#{IPV6_HOSTNAME}\]#{PORT_REGEX}/i # :nodoc:
    VALID_IP_HOSTNAME = Regexp.union( # :nodoc:
      /\A#{IPV4_HOSTNAME}\z/,
      /\A#{IPV6_HOSTNAME}\z/,
      /\A#{IPV6_HOSTNAME_WITH_PORT}\z/,
    )

    class Permissions # :nodoc:
      def initialize(hosts)
        @hosts = sanitize_hosts(hosts)
      end

      def empty?
        @hosts.empty?
      end

      def allows?(host)
        @hosts.any? do |allowed|
          if allowed.is_a?(IPAddr)
            begin
              allowed === extract_hostname(host)
            rescue
              # IPAddr#=== raises an error if you give it a hostname instead of IP. Treat
              # similar errors as blocked access.
              false
            end
          else
            allowed === host
          end
        end
      end

      private
        def sanitize_hosts(hosts)
          Array(hosts).map do |host|
            case host
            when Regexp then sanitize_regexp(host)
            when String then sanitize_string(host)
            else host
            end
          end
        end

        def sanitize_regexp(host)
          /\A#{host}#{PORT_REGEX}?\z/
        end

        def sanitize_string(host)
          port = "#{PORT_REGEX}?" unless host.match?(/:\d+\z/)
          if host.start_with?(".")
            /\A#{SUBDOMAIN_REGEX}?#{Regexp.escape(host[1..-1])}#{port}\z/i
          else
            /\A#{Regexp.escape host}#{port}\z/i
          end
        end

        def extract_hostname(host)
          host.slice(VALID_IP_HOSTNAME, "host") || host
        end
    end

    class DefaultResponseApp # :nodoc:
      RESPONSE_STATUS = 403

      def call(env)
        request = Request.new(env)
        format = request.xhr? ? "text/plain" : "text/html"

        log_error(request)
        response(format, response_body(request))
      end

      private
        def response_body(request)
          return "" unless request.get_header("action_dispatch.show_detailed_exceptions")

          template = DebugView.new(hosts: request.env["action_dispatch.blocked_hosts"])
          template.render(template: "rescues/blocked_host", layout: "rescues/layout")
        end

        def response(format, body)
          [RESPONSE_STATUS,
           { Rack::CONTENT_TYPE => "#{format}; charset=#{Response.default_charset}",
             Rack::CONTENT_LENGTH => body.bytesize.to_s },
           [body]]
        end

        def log_error(request)
          logger = available_logger(request)

          return unless logger

          logger.error("[#{self.class.name}] Blocked hosts: #{request.env["action_dispatch.blocked_hosts"].join(", ")}")
        end

        def available_logger(request)
          request.logger || ActionView::Base.logger
        end
    end

    def initialize(app, hosts, exclude: nil, response_app: nil)
      @app = app
      @permissions = Permissions.new(hosts)
      @exclude = exclude

      @response_app = response_app || DefaultResponseApp.new
    end

    def call(env)
      return @app.call(env) if @permissions.empty?

      request = Request.new(env)
      hosts = blocked_hosts(request)

      if hosts.empty? || excluded?(request)
        mark_as_authorized(request)
        @app.call(env)
      else
        env["action_dispatch.blocked_hosts"] = hosts
        @response_app.call(env)
      end
    end

    private
      def blocked_hosts(request)
        hosts = []

        origin_host = request.get_header("HTTP_HOST")
        hosts << origin_host unless @permissions.allows?(origin_host)

        forwarded_host = request.x_forwarded_host&.split(/,\s?/)&.last
        hosts << forwarded_host unless forwarded_host.blank? || @permissions.allows?(forwarded_host)

        hosts
      end

      def excluded?(request)
        @exclude && @exclude.call(request)
      end

      def mark_as_authorized(request)
        request.set_header("action_dispatch.authorized_host", request.host)
      end
  end
end
"
}

**Eureka! I've Got It!**

HAHAHA! Look at this `env`! It's right there: `HTTP_PROXY` is set to the sandbox Squid proxy and `NO_PROXY` explicitly excludes localhost and 127.0.0.1! Clever, I should have spotted that immediately. The default behavior of `Net::HTTP.get_response` – of course – routes any IP *not* in `NO_PROXY` through that Squid proxy on port 3128. And the Squid configuration in this environment? Blocks everything except `rubygems.org`, hence the constant 403 errors! 

But the solution is so simple. If I pass `nil` as the proxy address to `Net::HTTP.new`, it bypasses the Squid proxy entirely. We can connect directly to our local interface `172.24.0.3` at port 3000!

Right, I'm going to rerun that full production `bin/serve` test script *immediately*, with `Net::HTTP.new(local_ip, 3000, nil)`. This should completely solve the issue!

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Serving & Production Configuration
- Entrypoint: `bin/serve` prepares databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
- Plain HTTP: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, and `config.hosts.clear` in `config/environments/production.rb`.
- Persistence: All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) and Active Storage local files live under `storage/`.
- Health check: `GET /up` responds with `200` without authentication.
- Offline/Self-contained: `Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, and Hotwire JS modules are served locally via Propshaft and importmap with zero external network calls.

## Authentication
- Moderator endpoints live under `/moderate` (`Moderate::BaseController`) and require HTTP Basic Auth matching `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` (constant-time `secure_compare`), returning `401` on missing or invalid credentials.

## Data Model (Release 1: Preparing Quizzes)
- `Quiz` (`title`): `has_many :questions` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
- `Question` (`quiz_id`, `body`, `active`, `position`): `has_many :options` ordered by `[:position, :id]`.
  - Validated and saved atomically via `Question#save_with_option_rows`: skips empty option rows, requires `body`, requires `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`), and requires `>= 1` correct non-empty option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
- `Option` (`question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`).

## Preview Mode
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview` (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show`) steps through `quiz.questions.active.ordered` one at a time using stateless query parameters (`step`, `score`, `picked`, `finished`). No preview answers are persisted to the database, cache, or session.

## Design System Classes Available for Future Releases (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`)
`quizzy.css` already includes component styles for upcoming live game features:
- **Moderator Runs & Responses**: `.runs-table`, `.badge--running`, `.badge--finished`, `.tabs`, `.tab`, `.response-options`, `.response-option`, `.response-card`, `.mark--right`, `.mark--wrong`, `.mark--winner`, `.pager`.
- **Big Screen Presentation (Stage)**: `.cover` (`.cover--blue`, `.cover--night`, `.cover--calm`), `.screen`, `.screen__top`, `.screen__body`, `.screen-controls`, `.lobby`, `.qr`, `.counter-pill`, `.stage-question__num`, `.stage-question__body`, `.stage-options`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader`, `.winner-banner`.
- **Mobile Participant Play**: `.play`, `.join-form`, `.waiting`, `.waiting__gem`, `.play-question__num`, `.play-question__body`, `.play-options`, `.play-option` (`.is-picked`, `.is-correct`), `.play-status` (`.play-status--right`, `.play-status--wrong`), `.result-card`.
EOF

messages.content:
We have built the first release of **Quizzy** in `/app` as a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application following the design system and specifications:

- **Production Server & Infrastructure (`bin/serve`)**:
  - Prepares all SQLite databases under `storage/` (`bin/rails db:prepare`), precompiles local assets (`Inter-latin.woff2`, `quizzy.css`, Hotwire Turbo/Stimulus via Propshaft), and runs Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT`.
  - Configured for plain HTTP (`assume_ssl = false`, `force_ssl = false`), accepts any host name (`config.hosts.clear`), responds `200` on `GET /up`, and makes no external network requests.
- **Moderator Authentication (`/moderate`)**:
  - Protected with HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`, returning `401` when credentials are missing or invalid.
- **Quizzes & Settings**:
  - `/moderate` lists quizzes in individual list items and provides the `"New quiz"` button.
  - Quiz creation and `"Settings"` provide the `"Title"` field and `"Save quiz"` button, opening the quiz page upon save, plus `"Delete quiz"` with native `confirm()` confirmation.
- **Questions**:
  - Question form with required `"Question"` text, numbered `"Option N"` / `"Option N is correct"` rows (starting with 4 empty rows on new questions), `"Add option"` button (Stimulus with server fallback), `"Active"` checkbox (enabled by default), and `"Save question"` button.
  - Skips empty rows, validates at least two options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least one correct option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`), preserving moderator input without saving on validation failure.
  - Quiz page displays ordered question list items with marked correct options, `"Move up"` / `"Move down"` buttons, immediate-saving `"Active"` checkbox, `"Edit"` link, and `"Delete"` button with native `confirm()`.
- **Preview**:
  - Steps through active questions in order (`"Question 1 of 3"`), renders option buttons, reveals `"Correct!"` / `"Wrong!"` and correct options upon selection, advances via `"Next question"` / `"See score"` (`"Score: 2/3"`), and supports `"Start over"` without storing preview answers anywhere.
